speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how old you are and when you first noticed these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions fluid-filled and have they ruptured or left scars? Also, have you noticed any vesicles appearing in crops or a history of fever or cough?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for this viral infection, which aligns with the daycare exposure and contact with a sibling. No further tests or questions are required.
